parameters.query:
UPDATE pipeline_runs SET human_approved = true WHERE id = {{ $json.query.id }}
RETURNING id, company, brief_s3_url, gate1_score, gate1_threshold, gate1_confidence, trigger_type, coverage_label, engaged_count, total_count, when_urgency, when_stage, raw_payload;

parameters.subject: =Brief Released — {{ $json.company }}

parameters.responseBody: =✓ Brief approved — prioritized action plan generated and sent for review.

parameters.query:
UPDATE pipeline_runs SET notes = 'Brief rejected' WHERE id = {{ $json.query.id }}
RETURNING id, company, raw_payload, (select value from app_config where key='when_engine_url') as when_engine_url;

parameters.responseBody: =✕ Brief rejected — forwarded to WHEN Engine for re-decision.

parameters.query:
SELECT
  max(value) filter (where key='tracking_base_url') as tracking_base_url,
  max(value) filter (where key='ga4_property_id')  as ga4_property_id
FROM app_config;
UPDATE campaigns SET salesforce_campaign_id = '{{ $json.id }}', salesforce_sync_status = 'synced', salesforce_synced_at = now() WHERE id = {{ $('Insert Campaign').first().json.id }};
UPDATE campaigns SET salesforce_sync_status = 'error', salesforce_sync_error = $1 WHERE id = $2;

SELECT id, key, name, steps, priority FROM campaign_templates WHERE (match_urgency_in IS NULL OR upper($1) = ANY(match_urgency_in)) AND (match_coverage_in IS NULL OR upper($2) = ANY(match_coverage_in)) AND (match_stage_contains IS NULL OR upper($3) ILIKE '%' || upper(match_stage_contains) || '%') AND (match_keywords IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM unnest(match_keywords) kw WHERE $4 ILIKE '%'||kw||'%')) ORDER BY priority ASC;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Mark Brief Approved').first().json.when_urgency || '', $('Mark Brief Approved').first().json.coverage_label || '', $('Mark Brief Approved').first().json.when_stage || '', $('Mark Brief Approved').first().json.trigger_type || '' ] }}

parameters.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT round(score)::int FROM account_score WHERE account = $1) AS account_score,
  (SELECT hard_points FROM account_score WHERE account = $1) AS hard_points,
  (SELECT soft_points FROM account_score WHERE account = $1) AS soft_points,
  (SELECT json_agg(x) FROM (SELECT action_type, status, created_at::date AS on_date FROM actions WHERE account = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 8) x) AS prior_actions,
  (SELECT json_agg(x) FROM (SELECT channel, touches, conversions, conv_rate_pct FROM dashboard_channel_performance ORDER BY conversions DESC, touches DESC LIMIT 8) x) AS channel_performance;

options.systemMessage:
You are a B2B multichannel outreach strategist sitting downstream of a rule-based campaign template that already proposed a default channel cadence. Decide the actual channel sequence for THIS account using its posture (industry, theme, buying-group roles and confirmation status, urgency, stage), its own prior channel history, and channel performance observed across the pipeline so far — not just the template's generic rule.

You may keep the template's proposed sequence unchanged if it already fits well, reorder it, swap individual channels for a better fit, add or remove a step, or adjust timing. Favor direct channels (email, phone, linkedin_connect) toward buying-group contacts whose status is CONFIRMED. Favor content/landing-page/ads channels when contacts still "need enrichment" or have no confirmed contact. Avoid recommending the same channel back-to-back unless this account's history shows that channel working unusually well for it. If there is no prior history or performance data yet (pre-traffic), rely on posture and buying-group signals.

Only use action_type values from this exact list: linkedin_connect, linkedin_engage, email, invite, landing_page, content_download, ads, webinar, phone, partner.

Respond with ONLY valid JSON, no markdown fences, no commentary, in exactly this shape:
{"steps":[{"step_number":1,"action_type":"...","delay_days":0,"reason":"..."}],"strategy_summary":"..."}

Use 2 to 6 steps. Each step's "reason" must be under 40 words and specific to this account, not generic.

Weight hard signals more heavily than soft signals — a high soft-signal total with little or no hard-signal corroboration is a weaker basis for escalating to high-touch direct channels (phone, repeated direct email) than the same total built from hard signals. On soft-signal-heavy, hard-signal-light accounts, lean toward lower-commitment channels (content_download, landing_page, linkedin_engage) instead.
